description: Composite figure combining eight EBSD-derived geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) maps with three GND-density distribution plots for a duplex lightweight steel. The top row (a1–d1) maps GND density in the γ austenite phase at 0%, 1%, 3% and 6% strain; the bottom row (a2–d2) maps GND density in the B2 phase at the same strains, with austenite regions masked out as white. Every map has a 5 μm scale bar and all share one colour bar running from 10^13 (dark blue) to 10^16 m^-2 (dark red). (c1) marks austenite grains with dashed circles labelled G1 and G2; (c2) marks B2 grains with red dashed circles labelled G3 and G4. (e) and (f) are frequency-vs-ρ_GND histograms (x axis 0 to 2.0×10^15 m^-2; y axis frequency % up to 12 for austenite and 5 for B2) with Gaussian fits for ε=0% (green), ε=1% (red), ε=3% (navy) and ε=6% (magenta), each peak value printed. (g) plots mean ρ_GND (×10^14 m^-2) against strain for austenite (black circles) and B2 (red circles). Taken together the panels demonstrate co-deformation of austenite and B2: GND density rises monotonically in both phases, B2 starting higher but being overtaken by austenite at 6% strain.

observations.observation: All eight GND maps (a1–d1, a2–d2) carry a 5 μm scale bar and share a single colour bar spanning 10^13 to 10^16 m^-2, from dark blue (low) to dark red (high).
The GND maps are arranged in two strain-ordered rows: the top row is labelled γ (austenite) with panels (a1), (b1), (c1), (d1), and the bottom row is labelled B2 with panels (a2), (b2), (c2), (d2).
In the B2 row large areas are rendered pure white, i.e. the austenite phase is masked out so that only B2 regions are colour-coded.
The 0% strain maps (a1) and (a2) are dominated by dark blue, whereas increasing strain to 1%, 3% and 6% shifts both rows towards cyan, green and yellow, i.e. towards higher GND density.
Within the 3% strain austenite map (c1) two grains are highlighted with dashed circles labelled G1 and G2, and within (c2) two B2 grains are highlighted with red dashed circles labelled G3 and G4.
Histogram (e) is labelled 'Austenite' with y axis 'Frequency (%)' (0–12%) and x axis 'ρ_GND (m^-2)' from 0 to 2.0×10^15; a 'Gauss fitting' arrow points to the green ε=0% distribution.

Histogram (f) is labelled 'B2' with the same ρ_GND axis (0 to 2.0×10^15 m^-2) but a frequency axis reaching only 5%; printed peak values are 1.04×10^14 m^-2 (ε=0%), 1.18×10^14 m^-2 (ε=1%), 1.89×10^14 m^-2 (ε=3%) and 2.51×10^14 m^-2 (ε=6%).
In (g) the black austenite points lie below the red B2 points at 0%, 1% and 3% strain, and above the B2 point at 6% strain; the y axis is ρ_GND (×10^14 m^-2) and the x axis is Strain (%).
The legend in (g) identifies black filled circles as Austenite and red filled circles as B2.

The caption states that (a1–d1) are GND images of the austenitic phase and (a2–d2) are GND images of the B2 phase for strains of 0%, 1%, 3% and 6%, and that (e–g) are GND value distribution maps of austenite and B2 under different strains.

The citing text gives initial GND densities of 5.36×10^13 m^-2 for austenite and 1.04×10^14 m^-2 for B2 at 0% strain, rising to 2.64×10^14 m^-2 and 2.51×10^14 m^-2 respectively at 6% strain, matching the values printed in (e) and (f).

The citing text attributes the higher initial GND density of B2 to its smaller average grain size, and to residual dislocations from the relatively low 900 °C annealing temperature of the duplex lightweight steel.
The citing text states that the dislocation density of austenite increases more rapidly than that of B2 and surpasses it at 6% strain, which is the crossing seen in panel (g).

The citing text notes that even austenite grains (G1, G2) and B2 grains (G3, G4) of comparable size show different GND densities in (c1, c2), implying factors beyond grain size and crystal structure control deformation.

subfigures.description: GND map of the austenite (γ) phase at 0% strain; predominantly dark blue (low GND density) with isolated yellow/red spots, 5 μm scale bar.
GND map of austenite at 1% strain; still mostly blue/cyan but with more light-green grain interiors, 5 μm scale bar.
GND map of austenite at 3% strain; grains largely cyan/green. Two dashed circles mark grains labelled G1 (upper left) and G2 (right), 5 μm scale bar.
GND map of austenite at 6% strain; the densest and most yellow/orange-enriched austenite map, 5 μm scale bar.
GND map of the B2 phase at 0% strain; sparse blue/green B2 islands on a white (masked austenite) background, 5 μm scale bar.
GND map of B2 at 1% strain; B2 islands slightly greener than at 0%, 5 μm scale bar.
GND map of B2 at 3% strain; two red dashed circles mark B2 grains labelled G3 (upper right) and G4 (lower centre), 5 μm scale bar.
GND map of B2 at 6% strain; B2 islands show the most green/yellow of the B2 row, 5 μm scale bar.

Frequency (%) versus ρ_GND (m^-2) histogram for austenite with Gaussian fits at ε=0% (green, 5.36×10^13 m^-2), ε=1% (red, 7.44×10^13 m^-2), ε=3% (navy, 1.72×10^14 m^-2) and ε=6% (magenta, 2.64×10^14 m^-2); x axis 0 to 2.0×10^15, y axis 0–12%.

Frequency (%) versus ρ_GND (m^-2) histogram for B2 with Gaussian fits at ε=0% (1.04×10^14 m^-2), ε=1% (1.18×10^14 m^-2), ε=3% (1.89×10^14 m^-2) and ε=6% (2.51×10^14 m^-2); x axis 0 to 2.0×10^15, y axis 0–5%.
Scatter plot of mean ρ_GND (×10^14 m^-2) versus strain (%) for austenite (black circles) and B2 (red circles); no numeric data labels are printed on the points.
